beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Lands $900M Fleet Supply Pact for Vault II Cells
beats.body: Brunstone secured a five-year, $900M agreement to supply Vault II cells to a national commercial-vehicle fleet operator, its largest single order since the recall crisis. Frost called the deal 'proof the comeback is real,' noting it effectively resolves the demand questions that lingered even after the class action; the pact commits Brunstone to a third assembly shift by next spring.

beats.head: Castlestone Misses Badly as Grid-Core Delays Bleed Into Guidance Cut
beats.body: Castlestone posted revenue of $2.1B against $2.7B expected, with the relaunched Grid-Core campus still running at 60% of rated capacity months after Karsh 'drew a line.' The house slashed full-year guidance by nearly a fifth and disclosed that two anchor Compute clients had deferred contracts, sending Karsh into a combative call where he vowed the setback was 'the last one.'

beats.head: Fennvale Mfg. Ships First Auto-Parts Units as New Line Comes Online
beats.body: Fennvale confirmed first commercial output from its new auto-parts line, hitting the timeline Vossen laid out at groundbreaking. Initial volumes cover suspension brackets for two existing fastener customers, with management describing a deliberate ramp toward full utilization by year-end.

beats.head: Greenmarsh Agro Adds Second Blending Line to Meet Bundle Demand
beats.body: Greenmarsh committed to a modest second soil-blend line at its home works after the distribution pact pushed bundle volumes past existing capacity. Kessler framed the move as 'measured to demand we can already see,' with the line expected to reach output within three quarters.

beats.head: Halcrow & Vance Opens Third Yard to Absorb Swelling Vetask Backlog
beats.body: Halcrow & Vance commissioned a third earthmoving yard to service the combined $3.6B Vetask book following its recent follow-on mandate. Skarn said the yard adds roughly 30% to fleet-maintenance and staging capacity, positioning the house to bid adjacent regional infrastructure work as the flagship program peaks.

beats.head: Halcyon Industries Beats as Recycled-Fiber Grade Wins Early Orders
beats.body: Halcyon reported a modest earnings beat, with the newly debuted recycled-fiber packaging grade drawing faster-than-expected commitments from consumer-goods clients ahead of Northgate's startup. Ashby said two of Northgate's six planned lines have been earmarked for the new grade, calling demand 'stickier than we modeled.'

beats.head: Korrwright Works Debuts In-House Escapement as Halbrook Integration Bears Fruit
beats.body: Six months after the $1.1B Halbrook acquisition, Korrwright unveiled its first fully in-house escapement mechanism, ending decades of reliance on outside movement suppliers. Carrow told assembled press the milestone 'closes the last open link in our chain,' and hinted that a limited grand-complication series would follow within the year.

beats.head: Varnvale House Tops Estimates as Reborn Sovereign Line Clears Early Inventory
beats.body: Varnvale reported quarterly revenue up 14% to $840M, crediting brisk sell-through of the relaunched Sovereign line that Coyle staked her tenure on. Direct-boutique orders outpaced forecasts, though management cautioned that second-run production must keep pace to avoid the supply gaps that felled her predecessor.

beats.head: Boreas Power Strikes $3.2B Deal to Build Compute-Paired Power Campuses Nationwide
beats.body: Mira Thorne announced a $3.2B agreement with infrastructure partner Delmar Holdings to co-develop six power-and-compute campuses over four years, pairing Boreas storage with Halvane-built modules at each site. The deal, the largest in company history, locks in long-term offtake commitments Thorne valued at more than $9B across the contract life. 'This is the model we bought Halvane to build,' Thorne said, calling it the culmination of her acquisition strategy.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Faces Regulatory Probe Over Closed-Loop Reservoir Discharge Claims
beats.body: Regulators opened a formal inquiry into Greywater Grid's closed-loop water figures after inspectors flagged discrepancies between reported and measured discharge at two reservoir sites. The probe casts a shadow over the $2.4B compute pact anchored to those facilities, portions of which include performance clauses tied to water recovery. Sable Renwick said the company 'stands fully behind its data' and is cooperating, but acknowledged the review could delay site certifications.

beats.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Harbor and Corridor Awards Begin Billing
beats.body: Korrwright posted a beat on revenue of $1.48B, with the $420M Harbor redevelopment and $310M Corridor wire award both entering the billing cycle. Halden Fenn said combined backlog now stands at a record $2.1B, giving the group visibility deep into next year. Management nudged full-year guidance modestly higher on the strength of the structural segment.

beats.head: Thaldale Group Misses as Overhaul Costs Weigh on First Post-Scandal Quarter
beats.body: Thaldale reported revenue of $610M, short of guidance, as one-time charges tied to winding down the fastening unit dragged results into the red. Marta Holloway said restructuring costs totaled $140M this quarter and warned of continued pressure into the next, while insisting the cleanup is 'ahead of plan.' The restatement-related legal reserve was raised by an additional $45M.

beats.head: Vencyon Completes Modular Rollout, Debuts Unified Hub Platform
beats.body: With all five hubs now live, Iris Halloran unveiled the Vencyon Unified Hub platform, a standardized control layer linking sortation and retrieval across every site. The company said the modular buildout finished two months ahead of schedule at a total cost of $680M, and framed the platform as the foundation for its next growth phase. Halloran called it 'the payoff for four years of disciplined construction.'

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Documents Show Executives Ordered Kessel Fault Records Destroyed
beats.body: Internal memos surfaced in the widening probe showing senior Marlgear leaders directed staff to purge Kessel fault logs weeks before regulators arrived, according to filings reviewed at a public hearing. Dane Kessler denied personal knowledge but placed two divisional heads on leave as the board opened an independent review. Shares of confidence cratered as the class action added the document allegations to its complaint.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Strikes $2.1B Deal to Acquire Rival House Corriveaux
beats.body: Quinn Marrow unveiled the largest acquisition in Vossenspire's century-long history, absorbing storied timepiece and coachbuilding house Corriveaux for $2.1 billion. The deal combines Vossenspire's Thelvane case works with Corriveaux's renowned movement ateliers, creating a top-tier luxury conglomerate. Marrow said the integration would 'complete the vertical chain from raw brass to boutique.'

beats.head: Castlehold Lands Landmark $2B Grid-Storage Framework, Its Largest Ever
beats.body: Halden Voss secured a multi-year framework worth up to $2B to supply high-capacity modular storage to a consortium of regional utilities, more than doubling the firm's existing backlog to over $3B. Deliveries begin next quarter and will require Castlehold to accelerate a planned third plant. The deal cements Voss's aggressive first-year expansion, though it also raises execution risk given how fast the order book has swelled.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Ousts Petra Vandel as Reliability Settlement Forces Board's Hand
beats.body: The board removed CEO Petra Vandel after regulators finalized a $650M settlement over concealed reliability failures, the largest penalty in the firm's history. Directors named restructuring veteran Marcus Thorne as chief executive with a mandate to rebuild oversight and stabilize a shaken customer base. The exit closes a scandal that spread from shareholders to regulators over three brutal quarters.

beats.head: Blackhold Ordered to Idle Second Storage Campus as Probe Widens to Design Flaws
beats.body: Regulators expanded their inquiry into the overheating incident, ordering Blackhold to fully suspend operations at the second storage campus while investigators examine a suspected thermal-management defect across multiple units. The shutdown jeopardizes roughly $1.2B in grid-mandate obligations, and CEO Halden Dabney faces mounting pressure after acknowledging the campus was brought online ahead of schedule. Officials said the campus will remain dark until independent certification, with no firm restart date.

beats.head: Calderforge Cuts Guidance as Fourth Stormwell Hall Delays Compound and Yields Falter
beats.body: Calderforge missed a second straight quarter and slashed full-year guidance as the fourth Stormwell hall ramp fell further behind and next-gen tier yields came in below plan. Nadia Throne conceded the house over-committed on capacity ahead of demand, and disclosed a charge tied to idled equipment. The turbulent update marks Calderforge's sharpest setback in years, with Throne pledging a cost review across the Stormwell footprint.

beats.head: Drayton Freight Wins Continent-Spanning Warehouse Automation Contract Worth $900M
beats.body: Drayton Freight landed its largest-ever award, a $900M multi-year deal to outfit a national warehouse operator with pallet-lift handlers and material-handling systems. CEO Emil Holt, in a rare bold stroke, said the contract secures both assembly plants at full capacity through 2029. Management expects it to lift Material Handling revenue by a quarter next year.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Ousts Halden Roe as Storage-Bank Probe Turns Damning
beats.body: Vossenspire's board removed CEO Halden Roe after investigators found commissioning protocols on the failed grid-scale storage bank had been rushed against internal warnings. Director Mara Venn will serve as interim chair while the search proceeds, and the house suspended two further storage projects pending review. Shares have shed nearly half their value since the outage.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Hit With $900M Class Action as Veyra S Recall Failures Mount
beats.body: A consolidated class action seeking $900 million was filed against Brunmark Motors, alleging the twice-failed Veyra S battery fix left owners with unusable vehicles. CEO Iris Calvagh acknowledged the 340,000-unit recall remains unresolved and set aside a $250 million provision, warning the quarter would show a steep loss.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Lands Landmark $2.6B Emberline Supply Pact for Next-Gen Node
beats.body: Marisol Venn secured a multi-year commitment worth $2.6B to supply the newly unveiled Emberline node, the largest single agreement in Aperture's history and enough to fill most of the second fabrication site's planned capacity. Venn said the deal front-loads deliveries beginning next quarter and locks in a marquee anchor customer through 1959. Shares of narrative momentum aside, management now expects the second site to reach breakeven a full year early.
